_README: REAL PROOF ONLY. Nothing in this file may be invented. Every entry must be a real closed transaction or a real testimonial given with permission. The build check (scripts/check-content.mjs) counts PLACEHOLDER entries and blocks the launch check until they are replaced. Set placeholder:true on anything not yet verified. NOTE ON WHAT BLOCKS WHAT: testimonials needs a real quote and permission to use it, and nothing else. It does NOT wait on the Google Business Profile. Those are two separate tracks and conflating them held the launch blocker up for no reason: the GBP gates Google reviews and the local pack, it does not gate this file. See docs/review-request-campaign.md.

caseStudies.outOfAreaNote: This one was in Oak Ridge, up in Guilford County, not in Gaston or Cleveland. It's where Alec worked before, and it's the first house he bought and resold. We're showing it because the work is the point, not the zip code.
caseStudies.situation: Estate sale. A family member had passed away and the property was held in a trust, so title was clean and there was no probate fight to work through.
caseStudies.condition: Four or five cats had been living in the house. Cat urine does not just smell, it eats into everything porous it touches, and by the time we walked it the floors, doors, walls and carpet were all compromised. Add a pool and hot tub out of service, poison oak through the yard, rotted wood around the windows, three HVAC units needing work, a failed water pump, and cracked driveway.
scope: Floors torn out and redone to the baseboards; anything eaten away was replaced, then refinished
Whole house painted inside and out
Corkboard countertops replaced with granite; all bathroom stone replaced
Entire exterior pressure washed and bleached
Pool and hot tub returned to service
Rotted wood around the windows cut out and replaced
Three HVAC units repaired, water pump replaced
New outdoor living area built with lighting and a fireplace, plus a new path around it
Poison oak cleared from roughly two acres
caseStudies.size: About 5,000 sq ft on roughly two acres
caseStudies.outcome: Sold. The seller came to us because a family member had died and they needed somebody to take the whole problem, not just buy a house. They didn't clean it, didn't repair anything, and didn't deal with the cats.
caseStudies.lesson: The thing worth knowing: cat urine is one of the few conditions that can make a house genuinely unfinanceable. FHA appraisers are required to assess whether a property is free of hazards, odors and physical defects, and a house that smells like this one did will get flagged. That is why these houses sell for cash.

noSellerReviews._README: NOT PROOF, AND THE ONE EXCEPTION IN THIS FILE. Every other entry here exists because something happened. This one exists because something has not happened yet, and it is a disclosure rather than a claim, which is why it is allowed to clear the launch blocker when proof.testimonials is empty. A fabricated quote never clears it and never will. DELETE ON ARRIVAL: the day a real seller quote lands in testimonials, add it and set enabled false. This block is scaffolding with an expiry date, not a feature. See docs/review-request-campaign.md for the two texts that end it.
noSellerReviews.heading: We have no seller reviews yet
body: Zero, and we would rather print that than fill this space with something you cannot check. We have not asked a seller to review us yet, and we are not going to publish a review we did not earn.

That is a fair reason to be careful with us. It is also the reason the rest of this site is built the way it is. If we cannot hand you somebody else's word, we can hand you ours in writing with the numbers still attached.

checkable.text: One closed deal, written up in full, including what we paid, what it resold for and what we actually made on it.
Who Alec is, how long he has held a license, and the honest version of how much of that work is buying rather than selling.

noSellerReviews.heldBack: There is also a five star review of Alec's agent work on Realtor.com. We are not showing it anywhere on this site yet, because we do not have the link to the original and a review you cannot go and read for yourself is a claim. It waits until we can link it.
noSellerReviews.closing: If you sell us your house we are going to ask you for a review. If it went badly, say so. That is the only kind worth having.
noSellerReviews.short: We have not asked a seller to review us yet, and we are not going to publish one we did not earn.

agentReviews._README: DIFFERENT STANDARD FROM testimonials, deliberately. proof.testimonials holds private quotes given to us with permission. agentReviews holds PUBLICLY POSTED third-party reviews of Alec's agent work, quoted with attribution and linked to the original. That is honest only if the page says which it is and links the source, so sourceUrl is REQUIRED and check-content.mjs enforces it, an unlinked quote does not render. These are agent-side and out-of-area: they must NEVER appear in a city-page testimonial slot and they must NEVER clear the seller-testimonial launch blocker. Both are enforced in the build.

reviews.quote: My wife and I would highly recommend Alec Clausen to help a client purchase their next home. Alec went out of his way to help my family find a home when we needed it the most. We were living in Florida and Hurricane Ian damaged our house pretty badly. I called Alec and explained to him our situation, he immediately started sending us listings. We told him what we were looking for and explained that we have some health issues that make it difficult for us to travel so he said he would be more than happy to check out homes for us on our behalf. After numerous calls back and forth, Alec found us the perfect home! We bought the house sight unseen because we knew that we could trust Alec's judgment, and when we did finally go see the house, my wife started to cry she was ecstatic with how perfect the house is for our family.

team.bio: I got into business at eighteen, running Smoothie King locations. For eleven years my job was to walk into a store that was losing money, sometimes four at once, put the right team in, cut what was bleeding, and rebuild it from the bottom up until it turned a profit and the people working there were glad to be there. Same job now. The asset changed; the work didn't. I've been licensed since 2020, six years as a broker, and most of my experience is agent-side. I'm building the buying side now and I'd rather tell you that than pad a number.

marginDisclosure._README: Real figures from a real flip, published deliberately. This is the answer to 'you're going to make a fortune off my house' and it only works because the numbers are true. Do not adjust them to look better or worse.
marginDisclosure.headline: What we actually made on the last house we flipped
marginDisclosure.body: We bought it for $140,000 and sold it for $265,000. That looks like a $125,000 win, and it is the number people assume we're making on every house. We walked away with about $10,000.
marginDisclosure.why: The house needed everything. All the drywall, every bathroom, the roof, the water heater, every door. The copper had been stripped out. There was no refrigerator and no oven; they'd been sold. There was graffiti on the walls, holes in everything, and roughly 45 shopping carts' worth of debris to clear before we could start. Then, partway through the remodel, the water heater failed and flooded the house, and a good part of the interior had to be done a second time.
marginDisclosure.point: We're showing you this because the biggest objection we hear is that cash buyers make a killing on your house. Sometimes there's a good margin in one. Sometimes a water heater eats it. What you should take from it is that the gap between what we pay and what a house resells for is not profit, it's the cost of the work plus the risk that the work goes wrong. That's also why we'd rather show you the arithmetic than ask you to trust a number.

repairPadding._README: Alec's own figures from his own renovations. Presented explicitly as our experience, NOT as published data, because that is what it is. If a contractor disagrees, that is a fair argument to have and the page invites it.

rows.padded: broken out and each one pushed to the top of its range

repairPadding.pattern: The trick is not one inflated line. It is nitpicking every item and pricing each one at the top of its range or past it, so the total looks far bigger than the real number while every individual figure still sounds defensible.
